# GalactiLog-Windows Design Specification

Version 1. Status: source of truth for implementation.

Scope authority: the locked decisions from the user interview, 2026-09-09. Where this
document and the web application (the sibling `GalactiLog` clone, `docs/superpowers/TRACKING.md` section 1) disagree on scope, the
decisions win. Web source paths are cited throughout so implementers can diff ported
behavior against the original.

---

## 1. Purpose and drivers

GalactiLog-Windows is a native desktop port of the GalactiLog astrophotography session
logger. The web application is a SolidJS frontend, FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL database,
Celery worker, and Redis broker, deployed by Docker Compose.

Drivers:

1. Single-executable install on the imaging PC that already runs N.I.N.A. No Docker, no
   PostgreSQL, no Redis, no server process, no reverse proxy.
2. Single user. No authentication, no accounts, no API keys, no multi-tenancy.
3. Direct local filesystem access: reveal a frame in Explorer, open it with the registered
   application, copy path lists to the clipboard. A browser sandbox cannot do this.
4. Distribution to non-technical astrophotographers: one installer, silent delta updates.

The FITS and XISF files on disk are the ground truth. The database is a derived index that
can be deleted and rebuilt from a rescan at any time. There is no relation to the web
application database and no import path.

---

## 2. Hard rules

### 2.1 File safety

> The app NEVER deletes, moves, renames, or modifies any user file. Read-only on disk
> except the app's own data dir. No Recycle Bin feature. If a feature seems to need file
> mutation, stop and ask the user, then confirm again.

That paragraph is verbatim from the locked decisions and is not subject to interpretation.
Consequences implementers must not work around:

- "Missing files on rescan: delete DB rows, never touch disk." Deleting the row is the whole
  action.
- Relocating the thumbnail cache does not grant write access anywhere else. The relocated
  directory becomes app data; nothing else does.

#### 2.1.1 Two IO classes

Structural enforcement, per the design-lessons rule that security is enforced at the choke
point rather than by convention at each call site. Two classes, both in
`src/GalactiLog.Core/Io/`:

**`GalactiLog.Core.Io.UserFiles`** (class, not a namespace). Every read of a scan root or of
any path discovered by scanning goes through it. It opens with `FileAccess.Read` and
`FileShare.ReadWrite`, the share mode being what lets the application read a frame N.I.N.A.
still holds open. It has **no write members at all**: no create, no overwrite, no delete, no
move, no rename, no attribute or timestamp setter. There is nothing to call, so there is
nothing to forget.

**`GalactiLog.Core.Io.AppWriter`** (class, not a namespace). Every filesystem write in the
solution goes through it. It takes a destination path and throws
`UnauthorizedPathException` unless that path resolves under one of exactly four roots:

| Root | Set by | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The app data directory, the root resolved at startup, by default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\GalactiLogData` (section 17.2) | Fixed at startup | Database, WAL, logs, temporary files |
| The configured thumbnail cache directory | `general.thumbnail_cache_dir` | Frame, preview, and reference thumbnails, and the Sky view survey images under `survey/` (section 11.3) |
| One export destination, valid for one operation | A path the user picked in a save dialog, handed to `AppWriter.BeginExport(path)` which returns a scoped writer that is disposed when the operation ends | Two caller classes and nothing else: **exports of this application's own records**, which are the diagnostics JSON bundle (section 16.3), the log viewer's Save log as (section 12.8) and, from Phase 18, Export panels (CSV) on the mosaic detail page (section 12.17), written from `src/GalactiLog.App/ViewModels/Mosaics/MosaicDetailViewModel.cs`; and **generated scripts**, which is the stacking export's copy script (section 12.13). Every one of them writes one new file at the path the dialog returned; none chooses a path of its own, and none reuses the scoped writer after its own operation ends. |
| One staging root, valid for one operation | A folder the user picked in the stacking export wizard and confirmed on its review step, handed to `AppWriter.BeginStagingCopy(root)` which returns a scoped writer that creates directories and new files (`FileMode.CreateNew`) under that root and nothing else | One caller class and nothing else: `WbppExportViewModel`, the stacking export's in-app copy (section 12.13). |

The staging writer never overwrites, deletes, moves, renames, truncates or opens an existing file
for writing. A file already present at a destination is skipped and reported, as present with an
equal length or present with a differing length, and is never rewritten. A path carrying a colon
after the volume prefix, which names an NTFS alternate data stream, is refused. A reparse point
between the root and the leaf is refused. A drive root or a share root is refused as a staging
root. Sources are read through `UserFiles` only. **One limit is accepted:** a cancelled or
aborted run leaves the files that were in flight as partial files on disk. The result lists each
of them by path, and the application never removes them.

A generated script is a text file this application authors, in the same sense the diagnostics
bundle is: it is written once, to the path the dialog returned, and never read, re-opened,
executed or revisited. What it does when the user runs it is the shell's work and not this
application's, and the rule that constrains it is the generator's own contract, which emits no
delete, move or rename verb (section 12.13), rather than `AppWriter`'s path check. This
application never runs a script it wrote.

A fifth entry is one file rather than a root:

| File | Set by | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The data location pointer, `%APPDATA%\GalactiLog\datapath.json` | Fixed at `AppWriter` construction | The chosen app data root, and nothing else |

This is one file and not a root. `AppWriter.WriteDataRootPointer` takes no path, so no caller
can name a different destination, and `Authorize` still admits only the app data root and the
thumbnail cache root.

One further file is written outside the two roots, the export destination and the staging root:
the Startup
shortcut, `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\GalactiLog.lnk`. It is created
and removed by Velopack's own `Velopack.Windows.Shortcuts` COM API and by nothing else, from a
single file in `src/GalactiLog.App/Services/`, when the user sets `general.start_with_windows`
(section 12.11). It is not a user file: this application is its author, and the only mutations it
performs on it are its own creation and its own removal. `FileSafetyTest` confines every name in
that API to the one implementing file (section 2.1.3). Removing the shortcut removes any Startup
link to the same executable, including one the user made by hand: Velopack's `DeleteShortcuts`
matches by executable name and location, not by which link it created. This is a documented,
accepted limit rather than a defect.

`AppWriter` exposes create and overwrite of files it owns, and under a staging root the creation
of new files and directories only. It exposes delete only for files
under the app data directory and the thumbnail cache, which is what lets Serilog roll a log
file and the preview cache evict an entry. It **never** exposes delete, move, or rename of
anything under a scan root, and its path check makes a scan-root path unreachable regardless
of what a caller asks for.

#### 2.1.2 Third-party writers

Serilog's file sink, SkiaSharp's encoders, SQLite's native library, and Velopack all write
files themselves; no static analysis can see inside them. They are contained by construction
rather than by inspection: **every path handed to a third-party writer is produced by
`AppWriter`, never by a caller**. Concretely:

| Writer | How its path is constrained |
| --- | --- |
| Serilog file sink | Its path template is built by `AppWriter.ResolveAppDataPath("logs/galactilog-.log")` during `AppHost` startup. |
| SQLite | The connection string's `Data Source` is `AppWriter.ResolveAppDataPath("galactilog.db")`. The only place a `SqliteConnection` or `SqliteConnectionStringBuilder` may be constructed is `src/GalactiLog.Data/DatabasePaths.cs`, enforced by `FileSafetyTest`. The design-time migrations factory reuses it in read-only mode. |
| SkiaSharp encode | Thumbnails are encoded into a `MemoryStream` and written by `AppWriter`. SkiaSharp is never given a path. |
| Velopack | Writes inside its own managed install directory under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\GalactiLog`, which it owns, and, at this application's request, the one Startup shortcut section 2.1.1 names. Its shortcut API is reached from exactly one file and is given the executable name and the location explicitly, never a default. |
| Diagnostics bundle and log export | Both written through the scoped export writer from `AppWriter.BeginExport`. |

#### 2.1.3 Architecture test

`GalactiLog.Core.Tests.FileSafetyTest` scans the source of every non-test project (a Roslyn
syntax walk, or a plain text regex; the implementer chooses) for these call sites:

`File.Delete`, `File.Move`, `File.Copy`, `File.Replace`, `File.WriteAll*`, `File.AppendAll*`,
`File.Create`, `File.CreateText`, `File.Open` / `File.OpenWrite` / `File.OpenText` with write
access, `new FileStream` with any write-capable `FileMode` or `FileAccess`,
`Directory.Delete`, `Directory.Move`, `Directory.CreateDirectory`, `FileInfo.Delete`,
`FileInfo.MoveTo`, `FileInfo.Create*`, `DirectoryInfo.Delete`, `DirectoryInfo.MoveTo`.

The test fails if any of them occurs anywhere except the single allowlisted file:

```
src/GalactiLog.Core/Io/AppWriter.cs
```

`UserFiles.cs` is not on the allowlist, because it contains no writes. A new feature that
needs write access fails this test rather than silently shipping, and the only way to pass is
to route the write through `AppWriter` and inherit its path check.

`AppWriter.cs` is also the only file that may call `File.Copy`, which `CopyFileInto` uses for
the data root relocation (section 17.2), and a second pattern group forbids
`.WriteDataRootPointer(` and `.CopyFileInto(` outside `AppWriter.cs`, `DataRootPointer.cs` and
`AppDataRelocation.cs`.

A further group forbids the names `Shortcuts(`, `ShortcutLocation` and `ShellLink` outside
`src/GalactiLog.App/Services/VelopackStartupShortcut.cs`, which is the one implementation of the
Startup shortcut (section 2.1.1, 12.11). `VelopackLocator` is not in this group: it is not one of
Velopack's "legacy, stability not guaranteed" shortcut types, and
`src/GalactiLog.App/Services/VelopackUpdateChecker.cs` already names it for the update channel,
predating the Startup shortcut.

A further group forbids `.BeginStagingCopy(` outside `src/GalactiLog.Core/Io/AppWriter.cs` and
`src/GalactiLog.App/ViewModels/TargetDetail/Wbpp/WbppExportViewModel.cs`, the staging root's one
caller (section 2.1.1, 12.13). The exemption is decided on the full path, as the `BeginExport`
group's is, so a file of the same name anywhere else under `src` is still scanned. The new
`FileStream` the staging writer opens with `FileMode.CreateNew` sits in `AppWriter.cs` and is
covered by the blanket list above.

### 2.2 No webview

No WebView2, no CefGlue, no HTML rendering surface, no embedded browser of any kind. All UI
is Avalonia controls. Aladin, the sky viewer, and TradingView charts are out.

The Sky view window Phase 22 ships (section 12.4) meets this rule rather than reversing it: it
is a Skia-drawn viewport over still JPEG images the CDS hips2fits service returns (section
11.3), never a webview.

### 2.3 No authentication

No login, no users table, no sessions, no tokens, no role checks. The web application's
`require_admin` and `get_current_user` dependencies have no counterpart. Validation still
applies at trust boundaries: scan filter paths are confined (section 10.2) and the raw FITS
header query builder binds every operand (section 12.3).

### 2.4 Product scope only

This document specifies the product. Build process, agent protocol, task sequencing, and
review gates are not part of it.

## 3. Stack and versions

| Component | Version | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| .NET | 10 (LTS) | Long support window, single-file self-contained publish. Locked by decisions. |
| C# | 14 | Ships with .NET 10. |
| Avalonia | 11.3.x | XAML UI with no webview; keeps macOS and Linux possible later. |
| CommunityToolkit.Mvvm | 8.4.x | Source-generated observable properties and commands; no hand-written INPC. |
| Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite | 10.x | Migrations, LINQ queries, change tracking over an embedded file database. |
| Microsoft.Data.Sqlite | 10.x (transitive) | Raw `SqliteConnection` for the JSON header query builder and PRAGMA setup. |
| LiveChartsCore.SkiaSharpView.Avalonia | 2.0.0-rc5.x | Only mature Avalonia charting library; Skia renderer matches Avalonia's own. |
| SkiaSharp | 3.x (transitive) | Thumbnail encode and decode; already present via Avalonia. |
| K4os.Compression.LZ4 | 1.3.x | XISF `lz4` and `lz4hc` block codecs. Locked by decisions. |
| Serilog | 4.x | Structured logging. |
| Serilog.Sinks.File | 6.x | Rolling file sink under app data. |
| Velopack | latest stable | Installer plus delta auto-update from GitHub Releases. Locked by decisions. |
| xUnit | 2.9.x | Test runner. |
| Avalonia.Headless.XUnit | 11.3.x | Headless View and ViewModel tests with no display. |

Deliberately not taken:

- `System.CommandLine`. Four commands with positional arguments do not justify a
  dependency; a switch on `args[0]` covers it (section 15).
- Any FITS or XISF library. Both readers are hand-rolled per the decisions.
  `System.IO.Compression.ZLibStream` covers the XISF zlib codec.
- Any HTTP wrapper. `HttpClient` with a 15 second timeout matches the web application's
  `httpx.Client(timeout=15.0)`.
- Any DI container beyond `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection`, already present via
  the generic host used for configuration and logging.
- Any astronomy library for solar position. The sun altitude algorithm is 30 lines
  (section 8.4).

## 4. Solution layout

Four shipping projects and three test projects. The split is by dependency direction, not
by feature: `Core` must be usable from the CLI with neither Avalonia nor EF Core loaded.

```
GalactiLog.sln
  src/GalactiLog.Core/          no UI, no EF
  src/GalactiLog.Data/          EF Core, SQLite, migrations, queries
  src/GalactiLog.App/           Avalonia, ViewModels, Views, theme
  src/GalactiLog.Cli/           headless commands
  tests/GalactiLog.Core.Tests/
  tests/GalactiLog.Data.Tests/
  tests/GalactiLog.App.Tests/
```

### 4.1 GalactiLog.Core

Pure domain logic. References: `K4os.Compression.LZ4`, `SkiaSharp`,
`Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions`. No Avalonia, no EF Core.

| Namespace | Contents | Mirrors |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GalactiLog.Core.Io` | `UserFiles` (read-only user path access, no write members) and `AppWriter` (the only writer in the solution, path-confined). Section 2.1.1. | `backend/app/services/path_safety.py` |
| `GalactiLog.Core.Fits` | `FitsHeaderReader`, `FitsCard`, `FitsImageReader`. | `fitsio` usage in `backend/app/services/scanner.py` and `thumbnail.py` |
| `GalactiLog.Core.Xisf` | `XisfHeaderReader`, `XisfDataBlock`, `XisfImageReader`. | `backend/app/services/xisf_parser.py` |
| `GalactiLog.Core.Metadata` | `FrameReader` (static): single entry point that opens a frame through `UserFiles`, selects FITS or XISF reader by extension from `FrameReader.SupportedExtensions` (.fits, .fit, .fts, .xisf, case-insensitive), extracts metadata, applies NINA CSV backfill best-effort, returns rejection as data. Called by CLI `inspect` and Phase 4 scanner; no other code path reads end to end. `MetadataExtractor`, `ExtractedMetadata`, `NinaCsvReader`, `Provenance`, `Units`. | `scanner.py`, `csv_metadata.py`, `units.py` |
| `GalactiLog.Core.Sessions` | `SessionDate`, `AstroNight`. | `session_date.py`, `astro_night.py` |
| `GalactiLog.Core.Targets` | `NameNormalizer`, `CatalogPriority`, `AliasCurator`, `SimbadClient`, `SesameClient`, `ObjectTypeCategories`, `Trigram`, `StellariumNames`, `CommonNameOverrides`. | `simbad.py`, `sesame.py`, `target_resolver.py`, `target_helpers.py` |
| `GalactiLog.Core.Catalogs` | `OpenNgcCatalog` parsing. | `openngc.py`, `stellarium_names.py`, `catalog_base.py` |
| `GalactiLog.Core.Imaging` | `MtfStretch`, `Debayer`, `Resampler`, `ThumbnailRenderer`. | `stretch.py`, `thumbnail.py` |
| `GalactiLog.Core.Scanning` | `ScanFilterConfig`, `NameRule`, `FileWalker`, `ScanProgress`. | `scan_filters.py`, `scanner.py` |
| `GalactiLog.Core.Aliases` | `AliasMap` for filter, camera, and telescope canonicalization. | `normalization.py`, `equipment_aliases.py` |

### 4.2 GalactiLog.Data

EF Core over SQLite. References `GalactiLog.Core`.

| Namespace | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `GalactiLog.Data` | `GalactiLogContext`, `GalactiLogContextFactory` (design-time), `DatabasePaths`. |
| `GalactiLog.Data.Entities` | One class per table (section 5). |
| `GalactiLog.Data.Migrations` | Generated EF Core migrations. |
| `GalactiLog.Data.Queries` | `TargetListingQuery`, `TargetDetailQuery`, `SessionDetailQuery`, `StatsQuery`, `ActivityQuery`, `MergeCandidateQuery`, `DiagnosticsQuery`. Mirrors `target_listing.py`, `target_detail.py`, `api/stats.py`. |
| `GalactiLog.Data.Ingest` | `ScanCoordinator`, `ScanWriter`. `ScanCoordinator` has no Avalonia dependency; it raises `ProgressChanged` on the calling thread, throttled to 10 per second, and the App subscriber marshals to the Avalonia dispatcher. `ScanWriter` is the single sequential consumer of the scan pipeline's record channel (section 10.6). |
| `GalactiLog.Data.Repositories` | `SettingsRepository`, `CatalogCacheRepository`, `CatalogSeeder`, `OfflineCatalogLookup`, `CatalogMembershipMatcher`, `TargetRepository`, `TargetResolver`, `ActivityRepository`, `MergeRepository`, `ScanRunRepository`. They need `GalactiLogContext`, and Core has no EF Core reference. Each is a thin set of methods over a short-lived `DbContext`. `ScanWriter` calls them on its own long-lived context; UI actions call them on their own. |

Avalonia application. References `GalactiLog.Core` and `GalactiLog.Data`.

| Namespace | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `GalactiLog.App` | `App`, `Program`, `AppHost` (DI, configuration, Serilog, Velopack init). |
| `GalactiLog.App.ViewModels` | One ViewModel per screen and per reusable panel. |
| `GalactiLog.App.Views` | Matching `.axaml` plus code-behind. |
| `GalactiLog.App.Controls` | `SessionPane`, `NightStrip`, `MetricRangeFilter`, `FilterPill`, `FitsQueryRow`, `CalendarHeatmap`, `RawHeaderPanel`. `SessionAccordionCard` was retired in Phase 12 (section 12.4). |
| `GalactiLog.App.Theme` | `Themes/ObservingLedger.axaml`, `Themes/RedLight.axaml` and `Themes/GlassVoid.axaml` resource dictionaries, `Controls.axaml`, `Scales.axaml`, `ThemeManager`. |
| `GalactiLog.App.Services` | `WatcherService`, `ScanScheduler`, `ThumbnailCache`, `ShellIntegration` (reveal, open, clipboard), `UpdateService`, `DiagnosticsService`. `WatcherService` and `ScanScheduler` drive the coordinator from `GalactiLog.Data.Ingest`. |

### 4.4 GalactiLog.Cli

`GalactiLog.Cli` is a class library exposing
`CliDispatcher.TryRun(string[] args, Func<IServiceProvider> services, out int exitCode)`.
The factory is invoked only after a known verb matched; usage, unknown-verb, and --help
paths never build the host or open the database. If the factory throws, the dispatcher
writes the exception message to stderr and returns exit code 4.

`GalactiLog.App.Program.Main` runs, in this exact order:

1. `VelopackApp.Build().Run()`.
2. GUI switches (today only `--minimized`) are parsed out of `args`. The switch is consumed only
   when it is the whole argument list; any other argument list, including one that also carries
   `--minimized`, reaches the next step untouched (section 12.11 behaviours 1 and 9).
3. If any argument remains after that parse, call `AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS)` via
   P/Invoke so stdout and stderr reach the parent console and pipes (the App is a WinExe
   subsystem binary, which otherwise detaches). `AttachConsole` is skipped when the process
   already has a usable standard output handle (GetFileType of the stdout handle is
   FILE_TYPE_PIPE or FILE_TYPE_DISK), preserving redirected and piped output. Dispatch the
   remaining arguments through `CliDispatcher.TryRun` and return its exit code without starting
   Avalonia or acquiring the single-instance gate. `Program.Main` itself checks no verb list; only
   `CliDispatcher` does, through usage, unknown-verb, `--help` and known-verb handling.
4. Otherwise, acquire the single-instance gate (section 12.11 behaviour 1), build the host, and
   start Avalonia with the switch already stripped from the argument list.

One executable, one set of assemblies, same database path from `AppWriter`. The CLI scan verb calls the coordinator directly through `GalactiLog.Data`, so no interface is needed and no project reference cycle exists: App references Cli references Data.

### 4.5 Test projects

| Project | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `GalactiLog.Core.Tests` | FITS and XISF parsing, metadata extraction and CSV merge, session date and astro night, MTF stretch and debayer, name normalization and catalog priority, alias curation, scan filter verdicts, FileSafetyTest, the source-scanning architecture test from section 2.1.3. |
| `GalactiLog.Data.Tests` | Migrations apply on an empty file; every query in `GalactiLog.Data.Queries` against a seeded on-disk SQLite database; orphan pruning; merge and unmerge round trip. |
| `GalactiLog.App.Tests` | ViewModel behavior and Avalonia.Headless View smoke tests (section 18.3). |
| `GalactiLog.Cli.Tests` | `CliDispatcher` routing, exit codes, and stdout/stderr contract. xunit only, no Avalonia.Headless. |

## 5. Data model

SQLite, one file: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\GalactiLogData\galactilog.db`, under the resolved app data
root (section 17.2).

### 5.1 SQLite configuration

Applied on every connection open through a connection interceptor registered in
`GalactiLogContext`:

| Pragma | Value | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `journal_mode` | `WAL` | Readers do not block the writer during a scan. Locked by decisions. |
| `synchronous` | `NORMAL` | Safe under WAL; avoids an fsync per commit during bulk ingest. |
| `busy_timeout` | `5000` ms | Absorbs the brief writer lock without surfacing `SQLITE_BUSY` to the UI. |
| `foreign_keys` | `ON` | SQLite defaults foreign keys off per connection. |
| `journal_size_limit` | `67108864` | Caps WAL growth at 64 MB across a long scan. |

One connection pool, the `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite` default, shared by every context.

Concurrency contract, stated precisely because the looser version is wrong:

> **Exactly one writer during a scan. SQLite serializes everything else.**

During a scan, `GalactiLog.Data.Ingest.ScanWriter` is the only component writing. It owns one
long-lived `DbContext` and consumes the pipeline's record channel sequentially, performing
per record, in this order: image upsert, target resolution (offline catalog lookup, cache
read, online call if needed, cache write), target create if the identity is new, catalog
membership rows, activity events. Because that sequence runs on a single task, no two records
can create the same target concurrently, which is why the unique-violation retry the web
application needs is deleted here (section 9.7).

Outside a scan, UI-originated writes (notes, settings, merges, candidate dismissals,
maintenance actions) each open their own short-lived `DbContext`, write, and dispose. They
are rare, small, and human-paced. WAL plus the 5 second `busy_timeout` is what makes them
safe against a scan running at the same time; no application-level lock is used and none is
needed.

Reads always use short-lived contexts created with `QueryTrackingBehavior.NoTracking`.

Conventions:

- Identifiers: `TEXT` GUIDs, lowercase 36-character, the EF Core SQLite default. The web
  application's PostgreSQL `UUID` maps one to one.
- Timestamps: `TEXT` ISO-8601 in UTC with a `Z` suffix, format
  `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffffffZ`. Every value stored is already UTC; see section 7.1 for how
  an offsetless `DATE-OBS` reaches that form.
- Dates without a time (`session_date`): `TEXT` `yyyy-MM-dd`.
- JSON: `TEXT` holding one JSON object or array. SQLite JSON1 (`json_extract`) drives the
  raw FITS header query builder and is compiled into the shipped native library.
- Booleans: `INTEGER` 0 or 1.

### 5.2 images

Mirrors `backend/app/models/image.py`. PHD2 columns are dropped, and so is the web's mosaic
column `panel_id`: a frame's panel membership is a join, not a stored key (section 5.24). Phase 18
adds `panel_label` and the three geometry columns `ra_deg`, `dec_deg` and `width_px`, which the
web reads out of `raw_headers` at every detection run and this port stores once.

| Column | Type | Null | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | TEXT GUID | no | PK. |
| `file_path` | TEXT | no | Unique. Absolute path as walked. |
| `file_name` | TEXT | no | |
| `capture_date` | TEXT datetime | yes | From `DATE-OBS`. |
| `session_date` | TEXT date | yes | Section 8. |
| `thumbnail_path` | TEXT | yes | Relative to the thumbnail cache root. Reserved, and not written in v1: the cache is addressed by the recomputed key of section 11.3, so a stored path would be a second source of truth with no reader. |
| `resolved_target_id` | TEXT GUID | yes | FK `targets.id`, on delete set null. |
| `exposure_time` | REAL | yes | |
| `filter_used` | TEXT | yes | Raw header value; never canonicalized at rest. |
| `sensor_temp` | REAL | yes | |
| `camera_gain` | INTEGER | yes | |
| `image_type` | TEXT | yes | Raw `IMAGETYP`. |
| `telescope` | TEXT | yes | Raw `TELESCOP`. |
| `camera` | TEXT | yes | Raw `INSTRUME`. |
| `median_hfr` | REAL | yes | |
| `median_fwhm` | REAL | yes | Header `MEANFWHM` or `FWHM`. Provenance only. Never displayed, charted, filtered, or aggregated. See section 7.1.1. |
| `eccentricity` | REAL | yes | |
| `eccentricity_source` | TEXT | yes | `header`, `ellipticity`, or `csv`. |
| `altitude_deg` | REAL | yes | `OBJCTALT` then `CENTALT`. |
| `arcsec_per_pixel` | REAL | yes | Materialized at ingest. |
| `ra_deg` | REAL | yes | Phase 18. The frame's pointing right ascension in degrees, 0 to less than 360. Written by `MetadataExtractor` at ingest from `RA`, falling back to `OBJCTRA` (section 7.1), and backfilled for an older row by mosaic detection step 0 (section 7.7). Written together with `dec_deg` or not at all. |
| `dec_deg` | REAL | yes | Phase 18. The frame's pointing declination in degrees, -90 to 90. Written by `MetadataExtractor` at ingest from `DEC`, falling back to `OBJCTDEC` (section 7.1), and backfilled by mosaic detection step 0 (section 7.7). |
| `width_px` | INTEGER | yes | Phase 18. `NAXIS1`, the image width in pixels. Written by `MetadataExtractor` at ingest (section 7.1) and backfilled by mosaic detection step 0 (section 7.7). With `arcsec_per_pixel` it gives the field of view detection uses. |
| `panel_label` | TEXT | yes | Phase 18. The mosaic panel label parsed from `OBJECT` by the token rule of section 7.7, for example `Panel 2`; null when `OBJECT` carries no panel token and on every frame that is not LIGHT. Written by `ScanWriter` at ingest with the keywords in force for that run, and recomputed for every LIGHT frame by mosaic detection step 0, which writes only the rows whose label changed. Smart rebuild (section 12.7) does not touch it. |
| `hfr_stdev` | REAL | yes | CSV only. |
| `fwhm` | REAL | yes | CSV only, already arcseconds. The only FWHM any screen, chart, filter, or aggregate uses. Never multiply by plate scale. |
| `detected_stars` | INTEGER | yes | CSV only. |
| `guiding_rms_arcsec` | REAL | yes | Written by the CSV backfill (7.4) or by PHD2 correlation (7.6). |
| `guiding_rms_ra_arcsec` | REAL | yes | Written by the CSV backfill (7.4) or by PHD2 correlation (7.6). |
| `guiding_rms_dec_arcsec` | REAL | yes | Written by the CSV backfill (7.4) or by PHD2 correlation (7.6). |
| `guiding_rms_source` | TEXT | yes | `csv`, `phd2` or null. `csv` is stamped by section 7.4; `phd2` is stamped by the correlation of section 7.6, which never overwrites a `csv` value. The three columns above carry one measurement, so the source names all three at once. **Invariant: a non-null `guiding_rms_arcsec` always carries a source**, because both writers stamp the four columns together in one statement. A future writer that sets an RMS without a source would break the never-overwrite guarantee of section 7.6, since the correlation treats a null source as overwritable and would replace that value with its own. **Ordering within a scan, when `general.phd2_scan_enabled` is on:** the scan writer rewrites an image row's guiding columns from the file's own metadata, which nulls a `phd2` value when the file carries no CSV guiding, and the correlation later in the same scan visits that night and restores it. The two are ordered, not racing: section 10.3 runs the guide-log pass and its correlation after the header pass has finished. **With the key off that restore does not happen**, because the guide-log pass, the session time re-derive and the correlation do not run at all and no `phd2_*` row and no `phd2` value is written. A frame rescanned in that state therefore loses its `phd2` guiding value to the ordinary rewrite and keeps a null until the key is switched back on, at which point the first scan refills it: the stored guide data was never touched, and that night is then simply an unfilled night like any other. No `csv` value is affected in either state. |

| `adu_mean` | REAL | yes | CSV only. |
| `adu_median` | REAL | yes | CSV only. |
| `adu_min` | INTEGER | yes | CSV only. |
| `adu_max` | INTEGER | yes | CSV only. |
| `focuser_position` | INTEGER | yes | CSV only. |
| `focuser_temp` | REAL | yes | CSV only. |

Indexes: unique on `file_path`; non-unique on `capture_date`, `session_date`,
`filter_used`, `resolved_target_id`, `image_type`, (`image_type`, `session_date`),
`telescope`, `camera`, `median_hfr`, `fwhm`, `eccentricity`, `detected_stars`,
`guiding_rms_arcsec`, `focuser_temp`, `ambient_temp`, `humidity`, `airmass`, and from Phase 18
`panel_label` (`ix_images_panel_label`), which serves the available labels banner and the create
mosaic prefill of section 12.17. The three geometry columns carry no index: detection reads them
per target, through the existing `resolved_target_id` index.

The web application's GIN index on `raw_headers` has no SQLite equivalent. The header query
builder therefore scans with `json_extract`. Acceptable for a single-user library of tens
of thousands of rows. Known ceiling; the upgrade path is a generated column plus index on
whichever keys the user actually queries.

The app data root is deliberately not a settings key, because the settings document lives inside
it. It is resolved before the database is opened, from `GALACTILOG_APPDATA`, the data location
pointer, or the default (section 17.2).

The last two replace what an earlier draft put in a separate key-value table. They are
scalars on the settings document like every other scalar.

The three keys added in Phase 14B (`activity_seen_at`, `app_log_retention_days`,
`app_log_max_rows`) need no migration, for the reason section 5.8 already gives: a missing key
reads as its default, so a document written by an earlier version takes the defaults on its
first read and gains the keys on its first write. A stored value outside a key's stated range is
clamped to the nearer bound on read rather than throwing, and the editor that writes it refuses
the out-of-range value before it is stored (section 12.7).

The four keys added in Phase 21 (`astrobin_filter_ids`, `astrobin_bortle`, `nina_instances`,
`stellarium_instances`) need no migration for the same reason, and each carries its own reading of
a stored value the editor would have refused. A stored `astrobin_bortle` outside 1 to 9 is clamped
to the nearer bound on read, the treatment every other bounded scalar in this table gets. A stored
filter id that is not a positive integer is dropped on read, because there is no nearer bound that
means anything: an AstroBin id is an identity and not a magnitude, and clamping one would write a
different filter into the reader's upload. An instance whose `name` is blank after trimming, or
whose `url` fails the rule of section 12.16, is kept in the document and offered on no menu; the
tab still lists it, so the reader can see and repair what is stored rather than having it silently
removed.

The two keys added in Phase 22 (`survey_downloads_enabled`, `sky_view_survey`) need no migration,
for the reason this section already gives: a missing key reads as its default. Phase 24 turned the
switch's default on; every write of the `general` document stores the whole record, including the
first start's `catalogs_loaded_version` write, so a profile that has run Phase 22 or later holds
`false` and stays off until the reader flips the switch, while a profile that never wrote the key
reads on. Each key is written by its own control only: the switch by the
General tab (section 12.7) and the survey id by the Sky view window's survey combo, which stores
the reader's last choice so the next window opens on it.

**The three keys added in Phase 18** (`mosaic_keywords`, `mosaic_campaign_gap_days`,
`mosaic_position_tolerance_arcmin`) need no migration, for the reason this section already gives.
They live under `general` and not on a Settings tab: their one editor is the Mosaics page (section
12.17, ruling R3), which writes each on change. A stored `mosaic_keywords` entry is trimmed on
read, and a blank entry or a repeat of an earlier entry compared case insensitively is dropped, so
a hand-edited list cannot make the token rule match an empty keyword. A stored
`mosaic_campaign_gap_days` outside the seven listed values reads as `0`, the treatment
`default_page_size` gets, because a gap has no nearer list member that would mean what the reader
chose. A stored `mosaic_position_tolerance_arcmin` outside 0 to 600 is clamped to the nearer bound
on read, the treatment every other bounded scalar in this table gets. A change reaches the stored
labels and the suggestion list at the next Run Detection or the next scan, not at the moment it is
saved, and the page says so beside the control. `ScanWriter` reads `mosaic_keywords` once at the
start of a run, so a change made while a scan runs applies from the next run.

`default_page_size` (Phase 14C) is now written by the Dashboard pager's page-size select
(section 12.2), whose choice list is 25, 50, 100 and 250, in place of a value with no control
that wrote it. **The list is declared once** and the Settings Display tab's own select references
that one declaration rather than repeating it, so the two surfaces cannot drift apart. A stored
value outside the list reads as the key's default, 50, the same
treatment `general.theme` gets in section 14 for a theme id this build does not ship and
`target_page`'s four choice keys get in 5.8.2, rather than clamping to the nearest list member:
a page size has no ordering relationship to its neighbours that would make "nearest" a
meaningful fallback. That reading is **everywhere**, not only in the pager: the Display tab
normalizes a stored out-of-list value on load, so a document holding 10 pages by 50 and reads 50 on
both surfaces rather than paging by 10 while the Display tab shows 50. A change made on either
surface moves the other through one internal follow that
sets the page size and the select together behind a re-entrancy guard, so the write is one round
trip and the two selects cannot disagree.

Two things Phase 14B deliberately does not add here. The scan scope (all frames against light
frames only) and the orphan cleanup override are per-run arguments to `ScanCoordinator`
(section 10.3), not stored keys: they are choices about one run, and remembering them would arm
the next unattended run with a decision the user made once. `include_calibration` above stays
the stored default that the scope control starts from, and a run that overrides it does not
rewrite it.

**The three keys added in Phase 15A.** `phd2_scan_enabled`, `phd2_profile_map` and
`phd2_correlation_pending` need no migration, for the reason this section already gives: a
missing key reads as its default.

`phd2_correlation_pending` is **state, not a preference**. It records that a correlation re-run
is owed, so that a re-run which never ran is not forgotten across an application exit. It
appears on no Settings tab, no editor writes it, and a user never sees it; the Diagnostics page
may report it, and nothing else reads it but the correlation itself. Its rules:

- **Set to true in the same save** that changes a guiding time input, that is the normalised
  `phd2_profile_map`, `observer_timezone`, `observer_latitude` or `observer_longitude`
  (section 7.6). One save sets it once, whatever the number of changed fields. It is **monotonic
  under both writers**: `SaveGeneral` and `MutateGeneral` may each set it or carry forward
  whatever is already stored, but neither may clear it. Only the one door below clears it.
- **Cleared only by a compare-and-clear against the inputs the pass observed**, whether that pass
  ran inside a scan or out of one, through `SettingsStore.ClearCorrelationPendingIfUnchanged`.
  Each pass reads the general document once at its own start, before it waits for the resolution
  lease; that read is its snapshot. On completion the pass hands that snapshot back to the one
  clearing door, which re-reads the currently stored document under the write gate and clears the
  flag only when the same guiding-input comparison the setting rule uses finds no difference
  between the snapshot and what is stored now. A save that lands after the snapshot, changing a
  guiding input, is therefore never discharged by a pass that started before it: the flag stays
  true and the next pass visits every invalidated night again. This is why the flag needs no
  in-process generation counter or second gate: the comparison alone tells a late save from an
  already-observed one.
- **Left true** by a pass that is cancelled, that fails, or that is torn off by an application
  exit. A crash therefore loses no obligation.
- **While it is true**, the next correlation pass visits every invalidated night rather than
  only the nights the ingest touched and the nights holding an unfilled frame, and the
  application queues one out-of-scan re-run at GUI start (section 12.11).
- **Setting it raises no event of its own.** The save that set it writes `settings_changed` as
  any save does, and the re-run writes its own events when it runs. A key that quietly records an
  obligation must not add a second row to the feed for the obligation itself.

`phd2_profile_map` has one canonical shape, port of
`backend/app/services/phd2_profiles.py`, and exactly one normaliser,
`GalactiLog.Core.Phd2.Phd2Profiles.Normalize`. Every reader calls it rather than reading the
stored document directly, so the tolerances below exist once:

```
{ "Rig A": { "telescope": "Askar 120", "timezone": "America/Chicago",
             "latitude": 30.27, "longitude": -97.74 } }
```

- `telescope`: string or null. Null, empty or whitespace means the profile is not mapped to a
  telescope. The entry survives an unmapping when it still carries a timezone or a coordinate,
  so clearing the telescope does not silently discard the zone and the site; an entry that
  carries nothing else is removed from the map.
- `timezone`: string, default `""`. Empty means inherit `general.observer_timezone`. A zone
  name the platform's `TimeZoneInfo` cannot load reads as empty and inherits, and the pass
  reports the bad value once (section 10.9, `phd2_timezone_invalid`).
- `latitude`: double or null, default null. Null means inherit `general.observer_latitude`.
- `longitude`: double or null, default null. Null means inherit `general.observer_longitude`.

**Null is the only inherit marker for the two coordinates, never zero.** Zero is a legal
longitude and a legal latitude, so a falsy test against either field would move a rig on the
prime meridian to the observer's own site and file its nights under the wrong date. Every test
against those fields is a null test and `Phd2ProfilesTest` pins it from both directions.

Validation on read, applied by the normaliser and never by a caller: a non-string key is
dropped; an entry whose value is neither a string nor an object is dropped; a coordinate that is
not a number, or is NaN, infinite, or outside -90 to 90 for latitude or -180 to 180 for
longitude, reads as null and therefore inherits; a non-string `telescope` or `timezone` reads as
empty. A malformed entry therefore reads as an unmapped profile inheriting the observer zone and
site, never as an exception and never as a partially applied entry. The editor that writes the
map refuses an out-of-range coordinate before it is stored (section 12.7).

**Neither new key has an entry in `SettingsStore`'s write-path validator or in the read-path
range clamp** described above for the numeric keys. `phd2_scan_enabled` is a bool with no range
to clamp. `phd2_profile_map` is validated at read time and only there, by
`Phd2Profiles.Normalize`, which is the profile map's own normalisation and the one door every
reader goes through. Putting a second copy of those rules in the store's validator would let the
two disagree about a hand-edited document, and a document that failed a write-path validator
would take the settings screen down rather than read as an unmapped profile, which is the whole
point of the tolerances above.

The legacy web form `{"Rig A": "Askar 120"}`, in which the whole value is the telescope name,
is accepted by the normaliser and read as an entry with that telescope and the three other
fields at their defaults. This port never writes that form; the tolerance exists so a map
hand-edited from the web application's settings export reads correctly.

The map is rewritten in place when an equipment grouping renames a telescope (section 12.7):
only the `telescope` field of each entry moves, and each entry's timezone and site survive.

**The four keys added in Phase 16.** They need no migration, for the reason this section already
gives, and they appear on no Settings tab: the only surface that writes them is the Export for
stacking page (section 12.13). They are written on three occasions and not one. Save as defaults
writes `wbpp_exclusions`; choosing a staging folder writes
`wbpp_staging_path` on its own the moment it is committed, so a folder chosen once is remembered
without a second action, and that commit is the key's one writer, so a Save as defaults pressed
while the field is blank or refused cannot clear it; and every change to the quality filter writes
`wbpp_quality_by_rig` on its own. Each of those is one `SettingsStore.MutateGeneral`, and the filter's writes are coalesced
so that a threshold typed digit by digit is one save. `wbpp_default_os` is written by neither and
is read alone, from whatever the document holds. **The stacking export wizard adds no key**: its
method choice, its subfolder checkbox and its review are held for one run and stored nowhere.

**All four are tolerant on read, and the tolerance is structural.** None of them has an entry in
the write-path validator or the read-path range clamp. Instead **each of the four is held on
`GeneralSettings` in a form the deserializer cannot fail on and is read through its own tolerant
reader**, rather than being typed as `string`, `string[]` or a record and left to
`JsonSerializer`. That is not a preference: `SettingsStore.Deserialize<T>` has no catch, so a
value of the wrong JSON kind throws inside the settings read itself, before any reader could
correct it, and a hand-edited document would then take the application's start down rather than
one screen. The four readers give, in order: an os outside the set, or of any other JSON kind,
reads as `powershell`; a staging path that is not a string, or is empty or whitespace, reads as
unset; an exclusions value that is not an array reads as the nine defaults, and inside an array a
non-string entry, an entry empty after trimming and an entry carrying a refused character are each
dropped while the rest survive; a quality map that is not an object reads as empty, and inside it
a bad key, a bad entry and a bad constraint are each dropped at their own level. **No stored value
of any of the four, whatever a hand edit put there, stops this application starting**, and one
case per key pins that from a deliberately malformed document. **That claim is scoped to the four
keys' own values and not to the shape of the document around them.** `SettingsStore.Deserialize<T>`
runs at `JsonSerializer`'s default `MaxDepth` of 64, and a document nested deeper than that, or one
that is not well-formed JSON at all, fails before any of the four readers is reached. That is a
document-wide gap this port already carries against every settings key, not a property of these
four, and the four readers' guarantee begins at the point the document has parsed.

- `wbpp_default_os`. The script flavour the export wizard's method step preselects. A stored value
  outside the set reads as `powershell`, the treatment `general.theme` and `default_page_size`
  get above, and not a clamp: two shell names have no ordering that would make "nearest" mean
  anything. The value is a preference and never a detection: nothing on this port guesses a
  flavour from the shape of a path.
- `wbpp_staging_path`. The folder the generated script, or the in-app copy, copies into. **Null or
  empty means unset, and there is no default**: while it is unset the export wizard's staging
  folder step does not advance and asks for a folder (section 12.13). The value is not required to
  exist when it is stored; the script creates it, or the in-app copy creates it through the
  staging writer on the review step's commit and never before (section 2.1.1). Two rules are enforced before it is stored, in the editor and not on read: a
  path that equals, lies under or contains any configured scan root is refused, because a staged
  copy there is catalogued by the next scan as a second set of frames; and a path that equals,
  lies under or contains one of the export's chosen source folders is refused, because the copy
  would write into its own source. A stored value that has since come to breach either rule, a
  scan root added around it, reads back as it was stored and is reported by the editor when the
  page opens.
- `wbpp_exclusions`. The folder patterns both script flavours exclude, in order. The default is
  the web application's own list, verbatim: `WBPP`, `PixInsight`, `finals`, `WORK_AREA`,
  `masters`, `Masters`, `MASTERS`, `*CALIBRATED`, `CALIBRATED`. An entry that is not a string is
  dropped on read, as is an entry that is empty after trimming; an empty list is legal and means
  the scripts exclude no folder. A pattern containing a double quote, a dollar sign, a backtick, a
  backslash, a carriage return, a line feed or any character from U+2018 to U+201F is refused by
  the editor and dropped on read, because a pattern reaches both script flavours inside a quoted
  literal. The editor, this reader and the generator all ask the one predicate,
  `Core/Wbpp/ScriptGenerator.IsRefusedPatternChar`, so the three cannot disagree about the set
  (section 12.13 says what each character does).
- `wbpp_quality_by_rig`. The export page's quality filter, **kept per rig**, as the web
  application keeps it. The map is keyed by the port's one rig label, the telescope or `Unknown`,
  a slash, the camera or `Unknown`, which is the string the frame table's Rig column already shows
  and is never empty; `Unknown / Unknown` is a legitimate key with an entry of its own. The literal
  key `default` stands for a selection holding no frame at all, and is reached by nothing else
  (section 12.13 states which rig a given selection resolves to). Each entry is:

```
{ "Askar 120 / ASI2600MM": { "enabled": true, "baseline": "session",
                             "constraints": [ { "metric": "ecc", "op": "lte",
                                                "value": 0.55, "enabled": true } ] } }
```

- `enabled`: bool, default false. `baseline`: `session` or `rig`, anything else reads as
  `session`. `constraints`: a list of `{metric, op, value, enabled}` where `metric` is one of
  `hfr`, `ecc`, `fwhm`, `stars` and `rms`, `op` is `lte` or `gte`, `value` is a finite number or
  null, and `enabled` is a bool. Null is a legal stored value and means a chip the user added and
  has not filled in, which gates nothing.
- **A malformed entry means exactly two things**, and nothing else promotes an entry to the
  default: a value that is not an object, and an `enabled` member present but not a boolean. An
  `enabled` member that is **absent** is not malformed. The entry keeps its `baseline` and its
  `constraints` and reads the filter off, which is the default enablement anyway. A `baseline`
  outside the set reads as `session` and a `constraints` member absent or not an array reads as an
  empty list, and neither discards the entry: promoting either to a full default would silently
  switch a rig's filter off and lose limits the user typed. Recorded as a departure from the web
  application's own loader, which this port's reader does not follow member for member here.
- **Every degradation is local.** A missing map, a missing entry for the resolved rig, or an entry
  that is not an object reads as the filter off, the baseline `session` and no constraints. One
  malformed constraint is **dropped, not thrown on, and does not discard its entry**: a document
  written by a later build that added a metric must not wipe the other constraints when this build
  reads it. One malformed entry does not discard the map, so one rig's bad entry cannot cost every
  other rig its filter. A non-string key is dropped.
- **A write replaces one rig's entry** and carries every other entry through unchanged, so two
  rigs tuned in two visits both survive.

**Five of the web application's `wbpp_*` keys are not ported.** `wbpp_library_root` is not ported
because the scan root containing a frame is that frame's root (sections 10.1 and 12.13): the web
application needs it to translate a container path onto the user's own machine, and this port has
nothing to translate. `wbpp_quality_mode` and `wbpp_quality_score_threshold` are not ported
because the composite-score mode they configure no longer exists in the web application either:
its own filter module records the mode as removed, the modal reads neither key, and both are
written by nothing but the settings endpoint's own round trip. `wbpp_quality_enabled`,
`wbpp_quality_baseline` and `wbpp_quality_raw_constraints` are not ported **under those names**
for the same reason: the web application's modal reads none of the three and keeps the state they
describe in browser storage, keyed by rig. What they describe is ported, as the one per-rig map
`wbpp_quality_by_rig` above, which is the shape the web application's live state actually has and
the flat trio is not. All five are vestigial there and would have been dead on arrival here.

#### 5.8.2 display

```
{
  "groups": {
    "quality":  { "enabled": true,  "fields": { "hfr": true, "hfr_stdev": true, "fwhm": true, "eccentricity": true, "detected_stars": true } },
    "guiding":  { "enabled": true,  "fields": { "rms_total": true, "rms_ra": true, "rms_dec": true } },
    "adu":      { "enabled": false, "fields": { "mean": true, "median": true, "stdev": true, "min": true, "max": true } },
    "focuser":  { "enabled": false, "fields": { "position": true, "temp": true } },
    "weather":  { "enabled": false, "fields": { "ambient_temp": true, "dew_point": true, "humidity": true, "pressure": true, "wind_speed": true, "wind_direction": true, "wind_gust": true, "cloud_cover": true, "sky_quality": true } },
    "mount":    { "enabled": false, "fields": { "airmass": true, "pier_side": true, "rotator_position": true } }
  },
  "columns": {
    "dashboard": [ "name", "designation", "palette", "integration", "equipment", "last_session" ],
    "frames":    [ "time", "file_name", "filter_used", "exposure_time", "median_hfr", "eccentricity", "fwhm", "detected_stars" ],
    "ledger":    [ ],
    "mosaics":   [ "name", "panels", "integration", "frames", "date_range" ]
  },
  "sort": {
    "mosaics": { "key": "name", "ascending": true }
  },
  "dashboard": {
    "filter_panel_expanded": true,
    "filter_panel_width": 300
  },
  "target_page": {
    "grading_baseline": "session",
    "frame_list_format": "paths",
    "frame_list_mode": "good",
    "frame_list_include_unmeasured": true,
    "layout": "modes"
  },
  "analysis": {
    "tab": "correlation",
    "x_metric": "humidity",
    "y_metric": "hfr",
    "granularity": "frame"
  }
}
```

`groups` defaults are `schemas/settings.py::default_display_settings` verbatim: Quality and
Guiding enabled, the other four disabled, every field within each group checked.

`columns` is a map from table id to the ordered list of visible column keys. This is where
the dashboard's, the frame table's and the Nights ledger's column visibility persists
(sections 12.2, 12.4 and 12.15). A table id absent from the map uses that table's default list,
shown above; the third id, `ledger`, defaults to the empty list. A column key
present in the list but hidden by its metric group being disabled stays hidden; the group
toggle wins. One writer owns every `columns` list, `DisplayColumnWriter`, so a custom slug and a
built-in key are never written by two paths that could disagree.

`column_widths` (Phase 24 R5) sits beside `columns` and holds the widths the user dragged: a map
from table id to a map from column key to width in device-independent pixels, for example
`"column_widths": { "frames": { "file_name": 312.5 } }`. A fresh profile carries no key and
gains an entry only on a drag; the key is absent from the sample above for that reason.

  | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `column_widths.<table>.<column>` | number, at or above the floor | absent | The width the user dragged that column to. A column absent from its table's map auto-fits to the widest cell of the loaded rows plus its header, taken on every night change and column toggle. A stored width wins over the auto-fit until the user double-clicks the column's divider, which removes the entry. A stored width below the table's floor (48 for the frames table) reads as the floor; the drag cannot go under it. A table whose last entry is cleared loses its map. Only the frames table writes here today (section 12.4). |

The same writer owns `column_widths`, through the same load-modify-save, so a drag never
rewrites another table's or column's entry.

Notes.

- The 32 frame-table column keys are the `images` column names, in section 12.4's table
  order: `time`, `file_name`, `filter_used`, `exposure_time`, `median_hfr`, `eccentricity`,
  `fwhm`, `detected_stars`, `guiding_rms_arcsec`, `guiding_rms_ra_arcsec`,
  `guiding_rms_dec_arcsec`, `adu_mean`, `adu_median`, `adu_stdev`, `adu_min`, `adu_max`,
  `focuser_position`, `focuser_temp`, `ambient_temp`, `dew_point`, `humidity`, `pressure`,
  `wind_speed`, `wind_direction`, `wind_gust`, `cloud_cover`, `sky_quality`, `airmass`,
  `pier_side`, `rotator_position`, `sensor_temp`, `camera_gain`. `time` is the only key that
  is not an `images` column name; it is documented in the default list above and stays as
  written. The `groups` field keys are a different vocabulary (`hfr`, `rms_total`, `mean`,
  `position`) and stay as written here. The join between the two vocabularies lives in
  `GalactiLog.Core.Settings.FrameColumns` and nowhere else.
- On the default document 13 of the 32 columns are ungated and 19 are gated off. Ungated: the
  six columns with no group (`time`, `file_name`, `filter_used`, `exposure_time`,
  `sensor_temp`, `camera_gain`) plus the four `quality` and three `guiding` columns. Gated:
  `adu` (5), `focuser` (2), `weather` (9) and `mount` (3), whose groups ship disabled. 8 of
  the 13 ungated columns are in the default `columns.frames` list, so a fresh install renders
  8 of the 32 columns.
- Every frame-table column is hideable, unlike the dashboard's `name` column (section 12.2).
  An empty `columns.frames` array is a legal state that must not throw: the table renders its
  header row and the per-frame actions, and the column picker in the header is the way back
  out of it.
- `groups.quality.fields.hfr_stdev` gates nothing. Section 12.4's frame table has no HFR
  sigma column, and neither does the web application. The flag stays in the defaults because
  the `groups` defaults are the web schema verbatim, so the Settings tab (section 12.7)
  renders a checkbox for it that changes nothing visible.
- `dashboard` (Phase 14C, UI layout ruling 4) governs section 12.2's filter panel.
  `filter_panel_expanded` defaults to `true`; `filter_panel_width` defaults to `300` and is
  clamped to 220 to 480 pixels on both read and write, the read clamp being a member on the record
  itself rather than a rule each reader applies, so a hand-edited value outside the range
  cannot desynchronize the stored figure from the `GridSplitter`'s own drag range (section
  12.2, ruling E1). No migration: a profile whose document carries no `dashboard` key at all
  takes both defaults, the rule 5.8's own opening states for the whole document.
  Both keys record what the reader **asked for**, never what is on screen. Section 12.2's layout
  bound can render the panel narrower than the stored width, or as its 48 pixel strip while
  `filter_panel_expanded` is true, and it writes neither key, so widening the window gives the
  stored width and state back unchanged.
- `target_page` governs section 12.4's Target detail page. The object is per profile, like the
  rest of this document, and the document's existing extension-data rule applies to it the same
  way it applies to the document as a whole: an unrecognized key inside `target_page` survives a
  write. A profile whose document carries no `target_page` key at all takes every one of the
  defaults below, not only the ones it is missing. Phase 23 stage 1 retired five keys with the
  arrangement they served: `night_detail_expanded`, `frames_expanded`, `ledger_expanded`,
  `metrics_expanded` and `night_detail_height`. A profile that still holds them carries them
  through the extension data and they are written back unchanged. Phase 23 stage 2 added no stored key.
  Stage 3 added two: `layout` and `layouts` (the table below and the keys after it). Stage 4
  added none: layout D is a third value of `layout` and a third member of `layouts`.
- The four `target_page` keys are the Target detail page's grading and frame-list
  choices (section 12.4). They need no migration for the same reason the rest of the document
  needs none: a missing key reads as its default, so a document written by an earlier version
  takes the defaults on its first read and gains the keys on its first write.

  | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `grading_baseline` | string, `session` or `rig` | `session` | Which baseline the "Compare to" control selects for the frame table's sharpness and roundness grading (section 12.4). |
  | `frame_list_format` | string, `explorer`, `names` or `paths` | `paths` | The Copy Frame List dialog's output format. `paths` is the default because it is the format the page copied before the dialog existed. |
  | `frame_list_mode` | string, `good` or `bad` | `good` | Whether the dialog lists the frames that pass the grading or the frames it rejects. |
  | `frame_list_include_unmeasured` | bool | `true` | Good mode only: whether frames with no graded metric join the list. Ignored in bad mode. |

  A stored value outside a key's listed set reads as that key's default rather than throwing,
  the same treatment `general.theme` gets in section 14 for a theme this build does not ship.

  Phase 23 stage 3 adds two more members of `target_page`. Both read as their defaults on a
  document without them, so no migration:

  | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `layout` | string, a `TargetLayoutRegistry` key: `modes`, `bench` or `rows` | `modes` | Which arrangement the Target detail page shows (section 12.4). A value the build does not ship, including `tracks`, an unknown literal and an empty string, reads as `modes` and stays in the document until the reader picks a layout. |
  | `layouts` | object keyed by layout key: `modes`, `bench` and `rows` | `{}` | Per layout state. The one member is `lanes_height`, a number of pixels or null, the height of the lanes region above the frames table; null is the automatic rule. An unrecognized member of a layout's object survives a write. |

  An older document's retired keys, `guiding_expanded` and `guide_graph_height`, ride in the
  object's extension data and are written back unchanged.

- `analysis` is added by Phase 17 for the Analysis page (section 12.14). It has **four keys and
  no others**, and the page writes nothing else into this document or any other. No migration, for
  the reason the objects above need none: a profile whose document carries no `analysis` key takes
  every one of the four defaults, not only the ones it is missing.

  | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `tab` | string, one of `correlation`, `distributions`, `timeseries`, `matrix`, `compare` | `correlation` | Which tab the page opens on. |
  | `x_metric` | string, one of the ten X metric keys or the five PHD2 night metric keys of section 12.14 | `humidity` | The Correlation tab's X axis. |
  | `y_metric` | string, one of the ten Y metric keys of section 12.14 | `hfr` | The Correlation tab's Y axis. |
  | `granularity` | string, `frame` or `session` | `frame` | The filter bar's granularity segment. |

  A stored value outside a key's listed set reads as that key's default rather than throwing, the
  same treatment `target_page`'s choice keys and `general.theme` get (ruling A9). This matters more
  here than elsewhere: a PHD2 key stored in `y_metric` is a value the Correlation tab would reject
  at query time, and reading it as `hfr` is what keeps a hand-edited document from opening a page
  that cannot draw.

  **The four are the whole of what the page persists.** The Correlation outlier toggle, the
  Distributions mode, metric and grouping, the Time Series metric and smoothing, the Compare mode,
  metric and two groups, the equipment combination, the filter selection and the date range are all
  per visit. A date range in particular is a question rather than a preference, and a stored one
  would silently narrow the page on the next launch.

- **A `columns` list may carry custom column slugs (Phase 20, sections 5.19 and 12.15).** Every
  such slug begins `custom_`, which is a mandatory part of the slug rule and is what makes a
  custom key impossible to confuse with a built-in one: a custom column named "Name" slugs to
  `custom_name`, never to `name`. A slug in a list whose column has been deleted is inert, is
  dropped from the list on the next write of that list, and costs nothing until then. A built-in
  key is never given the prefix.

- **`columns.mosaics` and `sort.mosaics` (Phase 18)** govern the mosaics table of section 12.17.
  The built-in keys are `name`, `panels`, `integration`, `frames` and `date_range`, in that order,
  and all five are on by default; `name` is locked on, as the dashboard's `name` is, and the
  picker shows its box ticked and disabled. After them the list may carry the `custom_` slug of
  each mosaic-scope custom column the reader has switched on (section 12.15), which ships off.
  The table id is `mosaics`, and `DisplayColumnWriter` writes it like every other `columns` list.
  `sort` is a new object beside `columns`, a map from table id to `{key, ascending}`; `mosaics` is
  its only member. `key` is one of the five built-in keys and `ascending` a bool, default
  `{ "key": "name", "ascending": true }`. A stored key outside the five, a custom slug included,
  reads as the default, because a custom column carries no ordering this table sorts by. No
  migration: a document without `sort` takes the default. The writer is the mosaics table's
  header click, through `DisplayColumnWriter`'s load-modify-save, so a sort change never rewrites
  a `columns` list.

- **`columns.ledger` holds custom slugs only (Phase 20).** The Nights ledger's built-in columns are
  not hideable and are not in this list (section 12.4); the list names the session-scope custom
  columns the reader has switched on, and it defaults to empty, which is the user's ruling that
  custom columns ship off on the ledger. It is the one `columns` entry whose default list is empty
  by intent rather than by a table having no default.

**This document is read tolerantly, at the one read every caller passes through.** The rule is
that a member this build cannot read costs **that member alone**: it answers its documented
default and every other member of the document survives. A bare deserialize does not give that,
because `System.Text.Json` throws on a token of the wrong kind, and one such token anywhere used
to cost a profile its columns, its dashboard panel, its `target_page` disclosures and its
`analysis` keys at once, and the application did not start, because the startup read of this
document is what raised the exception. A stored literal `null` was worse, because it threw nothing
and handed every caller a null document.

The happy path is one deserialize and nothing else; the repair runs only after a read has already
failed. It uses the refused token's own JSON path to drop the member that path names, then reads
again, which is the case this section's opening already answers with that member's default. A path
matching no node, a document that is not a JSON object, and a document needing more removals than
the guard allows all answer the defaults whole. Each removal writes one warning naming the path.

**The guard is one rule at the document, not a converter per member**, for the reason design
lesson 2 gives: a converter per member covers the members that exist on the day it is written and
has to be remembered for every member a later phase adds.

**What a save after a partly unreadable read writes.** Every member that was readable is written
back unchanged, the member that was not is written as its documented defaults, and an unknown
member still round-trips through the document's extension data. **The raw text of the unreadable
member is not preserved**: it has no home on the document and a quarantine key for it would be a
change to this section's key list. That is a known accepted limit, and the warning is what stops
it being silent. A stored `null` **inside** a collection is not covered by the guard and is
answered on the record itself, which is stated so it is not mistaken for coverage.

**The other five `user_settings` documents still read through a bare deserialize**, and a
malformed `general` still fails the application at startup before any window. That is shipped
behaviour and is not changed here. The repair above lifts to them almost unchanged when a phase
takes it.

#### 5.8.3 graph

```
{
  "enabled_metrics": ["hfr", "eccentricity", "fwhm", "guiding_rms"],
  "enabled_filters": ["overall"],
  "default_chart_sessions": 1,
  "show_guiding": false
}
```

Defaults are the web schema's; `show_guiding` is the port's own (Phase 24 R3), the night
chart's Guiding pill, off on a profile that never wrote it. `session_chart_expanded` is retired since polish wave 6: the
per-session chart is always shown (section 12.4), and the key rides in an older document's
extension data, written back unchanged. `target_chart_expanded` is retired since Phase 23
stage 1, which has no collapsed trend band, and rides the same way.

Notes.

- The five graph metric keys are `hfr`, `eccentricity`, `fwhm`, `guiding_rms` and
  `detected_stars`. The graph document spells detected stars `detected_stars`, matching the
  web schema; the dashboard's metric range filters spell the same metric `stars` (section
  12.2.1) and keep that spelling. The two documents are separate namespaces with separate
  persisted histories and are not unified.
- `default_chart_sessions` is how many of the newest sessions the cross-session chart plots
  when it first opens. An "All sessions" toggle widens the scope to every session for the
  rest of the process and is deliberately not persisted: the setting is a default, per its
  name. The shipped default of 1 opens the chart on a single session, which is not a trend on
  this port's per-session X axis. A default of 10 or 20 would be more useful; changing it is
  its own decision, and the port implements the setting as written.
- The Display settings tab offers the value as a fixed choice list: 1, 3, 5, 10 and 20. The
  shipped default stays 1. There is no 0 choice: 0 would open the chart on nothing, and the
  scope is widened by the "All sessions" toggle rather than by a sentinel value in the
  document.

#### 5.8.4 filters and equipment

```
filters = {
  "<canonical filter name>": { "color": "#RRGGBB", "aliases": ["<raw name>", ...] }
}

equipment = {
  "cameras":    { "<canonical name>": { "aliases": ["<raw name>", ...] } },
  "telescopes": { "<canonical name>": { "aliases": ["<raw name>", ...] } }
}
```

The `color` key is optional. An absent key, a blank string, and the exact string `#808080` all
mean "resolve", not "grey": none of the three carries a user's intent, so none of them pins a
colour into the document. A raw name absent from every alias list is its own canonical name.
These two documents are the input to `GalactiLog.Core.Aliases.AliasMap` (section 12.2).

**Filter colour resolution (P13 R2).** `GalactiLog.Core.Aliases.FilterColor.Resolve` is the one
filter-colour resolution in the application. `AliasMap.FilterColor(canonical)`, which every
consuming surface reaches, and `AliasGroupViewModel.ResolvedColor`, the Settings swatch and
picker, both call it and carry no second copy of the order (HANDOFF 5.2 item 12). Nothing else
parses a filter colour. In order:

1. The stored colour for this canonical name, when it carries intent: not blank, and not the
   exact string `#808080`. Returned trimmed.
2. The seeded palette entry for the category the canonical name folds to
   (`GalactiLog.Core.Aliases.FilterCategory.Of`).
3. The seeded palette entry for the category the first of the canonical name's configured
   aliases folds to, tried in the alias list's own order.
4. `#808080`, held in `FilterColor.Fallback`.

The name fold is the web's `canonicalFilterCategory`, ported in `FilterCategory.Of`: it lower
cases the name, strips `_`, `-` and whitespace, and matches the result against one of seven
category name sets. It has no port analogue of the web's second step, "the stored colour for
the raw name", because every caller of `AliasMap.FilterColor` already holds a canonical name by
the time it calls it (`CanonicalFilter` folds the raw name first); step 3 above covers a group
whose alias, rather than its own canonical name, carries the category, which is the same ground
from the other side.

The seeded default palette, keyed by the category name `FilterCategory.Of` returns and held in
`GalactiLog.Core.Aliases.FilterCategory`:

| Category | Colour |
| --- | --- |
| Ha | `#c44040` |
| OIII | `#3a8fd4` |
| SII | `#d4a43a` |
| L | `#e0e0e0` |
| R | `#e05050` |
| G | `#50b050` |
| B | `#5070e0` |

**Deliberate divergence from the web.** The terminal grey stays `#808080`, this port's existing
fallback, and not the web's `#666666`. Changing it would repaint every unfiltered dot, tick and
swatch in the application for a difference nobody asked for.

**The `#808080` fallback is never treated as a stored colour**, in either direction. Reading: a
stored value equal to `#808080` resolves as though nothing were stored, because every build
before Phase 13 wrote that exact string into every filter group it created, unasked, so a
document holding it records an old default rather than a choice. The consequence is that a user
who wants a filter drawn grey picks any grey but `#808080`; `#7f7f7f`, for instance, is kept as
stored. Writing: `FiltersTabViewModel.SaveAsync` never writes `#808080` back as a stored colour,
so the document does not keep re-accumulating the value the reading rule discounts.

### 5.13 scan_runs

New in this port. The web application kept scan state in Redis
(`backend/app/services/scan_state.py`). With no Redis, live state lives in memory on
`ScanCoordinator` and durable history lives here. This table backs the diagnostics page and
the ingest history chart.

| Column | Type | Null | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | INTEGER | no | PK, autoincrement. |
| `started_at` | TEXT datetime | no | |
| `finished_at` | TEXT datetime | yes | Null while running. |
| `trigger` | TEXT | no | `manual`, `watcher`, `scheduler`, `cli`, `first_run`. |
| `state` | TEXT | no | `running`, `complete`, `cancelled`, `failed`. |
| `discovered` | INTEGER | no | Files seen during the walk. |
| `new_files` | INTEGER | no | |
| `changed_files` | INTEGER | no | |
| `completed` | INTEGER | no | Successfully ingested. |
| `failed` | INTEGER | no | |
| `skipped_calibration` | INTEGER | no | |
| `removed` | INTEGER | no | Orphan rows pruned. |
| `phd2_found` | INTEGER | no | Guide-log files the walk discovered this run (section 10.3). Zero when `general.phd2_scan_enabled` is off. |
| `phd2_ingested` | INTEGER | no | Guide logs parsed and stored this run. |
| `phd2_failed` | INTEGER | no | Guide logs that could not be read or parsed this run. |
| `error_text` | TEXT | yes | Set when `state = failed`. |

Index on `started_at` descending.

The three `phd2_*` counters are added by the Phase 15A migration (section 5.15) with a default
of 0, so rows written by an earlier version read as a run that found no guide logs.

Three of the guide-log pass's six figures are stored and three are not. `phd2_found`,
`phd2_ingested` and `phd2_failed` are columns because the Diagnostics page and the ingest
history read them back later; the pass's `skipped_unchanged`, `empty` and `removed` figures live
on the in-memory pass result and reach the reader through the `phd2_pass_complete` activity event
(section 10.9) and the CLI's scan output (section 15). A reader who wants a stored run to
reconcile therefore reads the run's activity event. The three are deliberately not columns: they
describe what one pass did at the moment it ended, nothing in the product reads them back after
that, and the event already records them durably. A column nothing reads back is schema kept for
its own sake.
