## 19. Deferred and non-goals

### 19.1 Deferred, verbatim

> DEFERRED (not v1): mosaics, analysis page (correlation explorer), WBPP
> export, custom columns, NINA/Stellarium integrations, API keys, Prometheus,
> backup/restore endpoint, sky viewer, filename-based target inference, fpack compressed
> FITS, light theme, any file deletion.

**The analysis page (correlation explorer) left that list in Phase 17**, which built the
Analysis page (section 12.14): the shared filter bar, the five tabs, the six read-only queries
behind them and the pure statistics in `Core/Metrics/Analysis.cs` that every figure on the page
comes out of. It is the whole of what the web's `analysis.py` and its ten components offer, with
the sixteen departures section 12.14 lists in one place, four of them the user's own rulings at
the approval gate, and it is a reader end to end: nothing on it writes a row outside
`user_settings`, and the four `display.analysis` keys of section 5.8.2 are the only thing it
writes at all. Phase 17 adds no migration and no table.

**Phase 17 also closes the longitude split of section 8.3**, which is the one part of the phase
that is not on the Analysis page: `Phd2Profiles.LongitudeResolver` gains the timezone fallback
`SessionDate.ResolveLongitude` already had, so a guiding session and the frames of the same
evening agree on the night they belong to (sections 7.6, 8.3 and 5.16). It answers HANDOFF 5.1
item 11e. It was taken here rather than carried because the PHD2 X metrics join on strict
`session_date` equality, so the split made them join nothing and say nothing on a library with a
zone configured and no longitude. It needs no migration: `phd2_sessions.session_date` is derived
and the existing re-derive corrects every stored row on the next correlation pass, with no guide
log re-read. The web keeps the split and this port departs from it.

**What the port does not take from it.** The Correlation tab's CSV export is not built. Writing a
file goes through `AppWriter` with a save dialog and a named `FileSafetyTest` allowlist entry
(section 2.1.1), which is a decision in its own right rather than an incidental button on a
read-only page; Copy Frame List (section 12.4) and Export for stacking (section 12.13) are where
that machinery lives, and adding a third caller is a separate amendment. Nothing else on the web's
page is dropped.

**WBPP export left that list in Phase 16**, which built the Export for stacking page
(section 12.13): the folder level rule with its contamination cost, the quality filter over the
checked nights' LIGHT frames, the totals, and the two copy script generators. What it delivers is
one new text file at a path a save dialog returned, written through `AppWriter.BeginExport`
(section 2.1.1), and nothing else on that page reads or writes anything under a scan root.

**What stays excluded from it.** The web application's in-browser copy is no longer excluded: the
stacking export wizard copies frames into a staging folder the user picked, through the staging
root that section 2.1.1 adds for it, creating new files only. File moves stay excluded on the same
ground as every other mutation of a user file (section 19.2), and neither script flavour contains
a move, a rename or a delete verb. `wbpp_library_root`, `wbpp_quality_mode` and
`wbpp_quality_score_threshold` are not ported (section 5.8.1).

**Custom columns left that list in Phase 20**, which built section 12.15: the Settings tab that
defines them, the one cell editor that serves all four surfaces, the cells on the dashboard target
rows and night expander, on the Nights ledger's night rows and on the session pane's rig label
rows, and the dashboard filter section with one control per column. It carries the port's sixth
migration, `custom_columns` and `custom_column_values` (sections 5.19 and 5.20), and it writes
nothing outside those two tables and `user_settings`: no file is read, written, moved, renamed or
deleted by anything on it (section 2.1).

**What the port does not take from it.** The web's `created_by` and `updated_by` columns are not
created, for the reason section 2.3 gives. `custom_column_values.mosaic_id` was created as a
nullable column with no foreign key, so that Phase 18 added the key, the cells and the fourth choice
and nothing else (section 12.15).
Twenty-six further departures are listed in one place in section 12.15, most of them defects the
port declines to copy rather than features it declines to build.

**The NINA and Stellarium integrations left that list in Phase 21**, which built section 12.16:
the External Tools tab that configures them (section 12.7), the two clients in
`GalactiLog.Core.Integrations`, the per-instance items on the Target detail page's overflow menu,
and the AstroBin acquisition CSV under that page's Export flyout. The phase carries no migration
and adds no table: its whole stored state is the four `general` keys of section 5.8.1. It reads no
file and writes none, the CSV going to the clipboard alone, and it opens no listening socket:
every call it makes is outbound, to a host the reader typed into the tab, so section 19.2's server
bullet is unchanged by it.

**What the port does not take from it.** The web refuses a loopback or link-local URL, resolves
the host before it calls, and reads an optional host allowlist out of an environment variable.
None of the three is ported, because all three exist to stop a browser persuading a self-hosted
**server** to call an address the browser itself could not reach; this port is the reader's own
desktop process, the URL comes out of the reader's own settings document, and NINA on the same
machine at `http://localhost:1888` is the ordinary configuration rather than the attack (section
12.16). The web's per-session-card buttons are not ported either: one menu on the target page
serves every instance, which is where the coordinates already are. The web's per-rig AstroBin
button becomes an automatic split rather than a second control, described in section 12.16.

**Mosaics left that list in Phase 18**, which built them as data and as pages: the four tables of
sections 5.22 to 5.25 and the four `images` columns, panel tokens and detection over names and sky
positions (section 7.7), at the end of every scan and on demand, and the Mosaics page, the mosaic
detail page, the Create mosaic dialog and the dashboard's mosaic link (section 12.17). It carries
the port's eighth migration and writes nothing outside the catalogue and `user_settings` except
Export panels (CSV), one new file at a path a save dialog returned, through
`AppWriter.BeginExport` (section 2.1.1). No user file is read for it beyond the headers a scan
already read, and none is written, moved, renamed or deleted (section 2.1). The panel arranger and
the composite image are the two later phases of the same plan and are not built here: the detail
page holds a placeholder band where the arranger goes, and its Composite button is disabled.

**What the port does not take from it.** The web's `needs_review` flag, its Needs Review pill,
Clear All Reviews and the Session Review banner (ruling R11). `images.panel_id` and
`mosaic_panels.target_id`: membership is a join of target, night and frame label against a
panel's nights, which may come from any target (rulings R19 and R19a). The `pixel_coords` flag (ruling R8). The suggestion
tile preview, which is the arranger in a read-only form and arrives with it. The toasts, the
page-local progress bars and the browser confirm and prompt dialogs, which become the job registry,
the Activity feed and inline confirms and fields (ruling R13). The settings tab: the three detection
settings live on the Mosaics page (ruling R3).

**API keys, Prometheus, the backup and restore endpoint, filename-based target inference, fpack
compressed FITS and any file deletion stay on the list**, and file deletion
stays there permanently (section 19.2). The light theme left the list in polish wave 6, which
shipped `atlas` and `logbook` (section 14).

**The sky viewer left the list in Phase 22**, which built the Sky view button and window of
section 12.4 over the hips2fits client of section 11.3. It carries no migration and adds no table;
its stored state is the two `general` keys of section 5.8.1 and the image files under `survey/`.
Departures from the web: **still images, not Aladin**, because section 2.2 admits no webview, so
the window fetches a new JPEG for each pan and zoom where Aladin streams tiles; **one host**,
hips2fits, where the web used Aladin's tile servers and NASA SkyView, the DSS cutout being
hips2fits at `P/DSS2/red` and the default field; **no reference toggle**, because the target
header carries no reference thumbnail and no survey image is ever one (section 11.4); **the field
is clamped** to 0.1 and 5.0 degrees for every view, where the web clamped it only for SkyView and
opened Aladin at an unclamped field; **15 seconds**, not the web's 30, for the fetch; and **fetched
on demand**, one view at a time while the window is open and the switch is on, where the web
fetched a cutout for every target in a background worker.

PHD2 guiding left that list in Phase 15A, which built the data path: discovery, parsing,
storage, the profile map and the per-frame correlation (sections 5.15 to 5.18, 7.6, 10.3, 12.7),
and the provenance mark on the Target detail page (section 12.4).

**What Phase 15B delivers**, all of it a reader over the tables Phase 15A filled: the "Guiding"
section on the night pane with its rollup, its calibration chips and its guide graph (section
12.4; since Phase 24 R3 the rollup and the graph are the night chart's Guiding pill and the chips
are gone), the two `display.target_page` keys that section persists (section 5.8.2), the Guiding
section on the Statistics page with the per-rig scorecard and the altitude arcs (section 12.5),
and the two drawn controls both need (section 13). It ports `phd2_stats.py`, the cross-night
aggregates, as `GuidingStatsQuery` behind the Statistics section. Nothing in that list writes a
`phd2_*` row or an `images` guiding column, and nothing in it is written outside `user_settings`.

**Phase 15B also closes two carried items on the write side**, which is the one part of the phase
that is not a reader: `phd2_sessions.ended_at_local` and the end re-derive built on it, and the
clear-side hold-out for an unzoned session (sections 5.16 and 7.6). They carry the port's fifth
migration, which adds that one column. They were carried because the phase was planned with no
migration; the application has not shipped, every install is a new one until `main` releases run
through the release workflow of section 17.5, and a schema change is therefore not a reason to
defer a correctness fix.

**`phd2_sidereal.py` is not ported by Phase 15B and is now unowned.** It is the sidereal
cross-check that solves a rig's longitude from the pointing line and warns when the configured
timezone disagrees with it. It is an ingest-time warning over a guide log's header, not a
surface: it belongs beside the log's own header parse and the `phd2_timezone_unset` event of
section 10.9, and Phase 15B opens neither. Its two carried items above open the correlation's
re-derive, which consumes a resolved zone; they do not open the parse that would have to read a
pointing line, nor the warning that would have to report a disagreement. The phase's task
table carries no task for it, the roadmap's Phase 15B section does not name it, and folding 548
lines of GMST arithmetic and its verdict thresholds into a view phase to satisfy a sentence
written in Phase 15A would be the wrong reason to build it. It stays deferred, and the phase
that next opens the guide-log ingest path is where it is decided.

### 19.2 Explicit non-goals

Not deferred, not planned, and not to be added without a new decision:

- Any embedded browser or HTML rendering surface.
- Authentication, user accounts, roles, or multi-user support.
- Any server, listening socket, or remote API. Phase 21's integrations do not touch this bullet:
  GalactiLog is a client of NINA and of Stellarium and never the other way round, so it binds no
  port, accepts no connection and exposes no endpoint, and the two protocols of section 12.16 are
  outbound HTTP calls to a host the reader configured and to nothing else. A request to let an
  external tool call **into** GalactiLog is this bullet, and needs a new decision.
- Docker, PostgreSQL, Redis, or an external message broker.
- Importing from, or synchronizing with, the web application's database.
- Writing, moving, renaming, or deleting any user file, including a "clean up" or "organize
  library" feature, and including a Recycle Bin. See section 2.1.
- Downloading survey images (SkyView, DSS) for reference thumbnails. Reference thumbnails
  come from the user's own frames (section 11.4). The Sky view window's hips2fits images
  (sections 11.3 and 12.4) are session imagery for that window and never a reference thumbnail.
- macOS and Linux builds. Avalonia keeps the option open; no CI targets them and no
  platform-specific path in `ShellIntegration` is written for them beyond the guard that
  reveals the code path is Windows-only.
- Cloud sync, telemetry, or crash reporting to a remote endpoint.

---

## 20. Open questions

None. The three questions this document carried in its first revision were answered in the
review pass and the answers are now specified in place:

| Question | Answer | Where it now lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reference thumbnail source | Generated from the target's own most recent LIGHT frame. No survey image is ever the reference; the Sky view window's images are session imagery. | 11.4, 12.4, 19.2 |
| Metric range filter semantics | Per frame, every frame must be in range. Not the group average. | 12.2.1 |
| Log level setting | `general.log_level`, default `Information`, exposed only on the Diagnostics tab. | 5.8.1, 12.7, 16.1 |

Nothing new was raised while applying the review. Anything an implementer finds ambiguous
from here is a spec defect: raise it rather than guessing, particularly anywhere section 2.1
or section 5.1 is involved.
